result.summary: Replaces nullable `std::unique_ptr` with `util::NotNullUniquePtr` (or plain references) for `CreateNewBlock`, `CreateNewTemplate`, and pimpl members across several subsystems (`AddrMan`, `MuSig2SecNonce`, `TxDownloadManager`, `TxReconciliationTracker`, `TxRequestTracker`, and `CDBWrapper`). It drops redundant null checks and assertions at call sites across tests, mining RPCs, and fee estimation, and expands `NotNull` unit tests with conversion and type-trait checks.
result.problem: Pointers that are guaranteed never to be null are typed as standard nullable smart pointers. This obscures the API contract, leaves reviewers unsure whether pointers can be null, and produces dead error-handling branches in test coverage and mutation testing.
evidence: Author notes in the description that 'Pointers that are never null still have confusing null checks (with possible error handling return branches), which are always dead in coverage reports or when applying mutation testing.'
Author notes in commit messages that the pimpl and test changes were suggested during review of PR #34844.
result.card: Replaces nullable smart pointers with util::NotNullUniquePtr for CreateNewBlock, CreateNewTemplate, and several internal pimpl members across the codebase. Currently, pointers guaranteed to be non-null are exposed as nullable pointers, prompting redundant null checks and dead error-handling branches. The author notes that compile-time non-null guarantees clarify API contracts and eliminate dead branches from coverage and mutation testing reports. No dependencies are declared.

risk.why: If block template generation unexpectedly returned a null pointer, removing the runtime error checks and wrapping in NotNull would cause an immediate crash or assertion failure instead of an error response.
